title: Sticky session prefetch profiles and SDK ergonomics (PRD draft)
content:
Context and motivation:

We continue to see customer requests for predictable latency with transitive tool-calls (search, SQL, code-exec) while minimizing unit cost. Currently Hosted API streaming exposes two orthogonal levers: (1) client-side session affinity (session_id + warmup requests), and (2) speculative prefetch on the server. Both are powerfully useful but brittle in practice for embedded SDKs: clients either over-prefetch (waste) or under-prefetch (cold tool latency).

This PRD sketches a focused feature: Sticky Session Prefetch Profiles — a lightweight, server-coordinated set of prefetch/keepalive policies that SDKs can opt into. Goal: enable low-latency tool-calls and structured partial-outputs for medium-length interactive sessions (avg. 5-40 turns) while keeping steady-state token cost predictable.

High-level goals:
- Deliver median tool-call latency reduction of at least 25% for sessions that opt into a profile, relative to baseline cold tool invocation.
- Keep incremental cost growth < 12% for workloads with average session length in target range.
- Provide ergonomic SDK surface: one-line opt-in and clear telemetry hooks for developers.
- Avoid global pinning: sessions should be sticky within a region/cluster and gracefully fallback if capacity constrained.

Non-goals:
- Replacing Dedicated/reserved capacity behavior. Sticky profiles are a hosted-layer optimization, not a reserved-customer contract.
- Vertical autoscaling changes to GPU fleet. We will rely on existing autoscaler signals and only add hints.

User personas and stories:
- Product engineer (mobile chat app): "I want tool calls to feel instant when users converse over a 10-turn help session, but I cannot blow up my costs."
- Platform engineer (internal): "I need hooks to debug why a session moved off-hot routing and to decide whether to rehydrate caches."
- SDK author: "I want a simple API that I can call once at session creation, and then be able to observe prefetch effects via telemetry."

Success metrics (measured over 30d experiment cohorts):
- Latency: median tool-call p50 reduced by >= 25% for opt-in sessions, p95 improved by >= 10%.
- Cost: per-session token-equivalent cost increase <= 12% for target workloads.
- Adoption: >= 20% of new SDK sessions in the beta group opt into a sticky profile within 6 weeks of launch.
- Reliability: session fallbacks (hot -> cold) occur < 1% of requests for opt-in sessions during normal load.

Design overview:
- Profile concepts: profile_id identifies a prefetch/keepalive policy. Each profile carries parameters (prefetch_depth, keepalive_ttl, tool_warm_targets) and behavioral hints (allow_burst, regional_affinity). Profiles are server-native objects — clients reference profile_id when creating sessions.
- Lifecycle: SDK creates a session with profile_id. The control plane routes that session to a hot-serving shard. The serving runtime uses profile hints to prewarm tool runtimes and KV caches, and to keep per-session worker/allocations alive for keepalive_ttl. If resources constrained, the router may evict sessions and set a short-lived sticky_cookie explaining reason.
- Streaming + partial structured outputs: streaming tokens may include a light session header indicating prefetch progress and active tool bindings. This enables client UI to show a progressive "tool warm" indicator and also to match structured output frames to tool availability.

API / SDK surface sketches:
- REST creation (example):
  POST /v1/sessions
  {
    "model": "rw-stream-1",
    "profile_id": "sticky-medium-1",
    "prefetch_goals": ["search", "db"],
    "session_metadata": {"app": "support-chat"}
  }
  Response: { session_id, region, sticky_cookie, profile_applied }

- SDK (pseudo JS):
  // one-line opt-in on session start
  const s = await client.sessions.create({ model: 'rw-stream-1', profile: 'sticky-medium-1' })

  // telemetry: attach event hooks
  client.on('session.warm', (meta) => showWarmIndicator())
  client.on('session.evicted', (reason) => metrics.increment('session.evicted', reason))

- Backoff/fallback semantics: when a call observes sticky_cookie == 'evicted' or profile_applied == false, SDK should automatically degrade to non-prefetch path and surface a soft latency SLO warning if configured.

Prefetch profiles (initial set):
- sticky-light (prefetch_depth=1, keepalive_ttl=20s, tool_warm_targets=[search])
- sticky-medium (prefetch_depth=3, keepalive_ttl=60s, tool_warm_targets=[search, llm-embed])
- sticky-heavy (prefetch_depth=6, keepalive_ttl=180s, tool_warm_targets=[search, db, code-runner])

Server behavior and knobs:
- Prefetch: server runs speculative inferences to materialize required KV cache segments and warms up tool containers (cold-start mitigations) up to prefetch_depth tokens average. Prefetch work is throttled by allow_burst flag and global capacity budget.
- Keepalive: ephemeral allocations are kept reserved for keepalive_ttl after last activity. Keepalive accounting aggregates per-profile budgets and will evict LRU sessions when limits hit.
- Telemetry: session-level metrics emitted: session.warm_start, session.prefetch_tokens, session.keepalive_evictions, session.hot_routed=true/false, tool_warm_time_ms. These should be available in Console per-session and aggregated by profile.

SDK ergonomics guidance:
- Default opt-in: SDKs should default to off for web-first use cases; mobile and desktop SDKs may enable sticky-medium by default in the beta channel.
- Minimal surface: session.create(profile_id) and one optional config object for telemetry. Avoid forcing customers to choose low-level knobs.
- UI guidance: expose a non-blocking warm indicator and an optional detailed overlay (dev mode) with session status and last evict reason.

Observability and SLOs:
- New traces: annotate traces with session.profile_id, session.hot_routed boolean, prefetch_tokens, and tool_warm_time.
- Dashboards: per-profile latency and cost graphs, hot->cold transitions over time, and percent of sessions evicted under load.
- Alerts: trigger if session.evictions > 0.5% of requests for opt-in profiles or if p95 tool_warm_time > 300ms for sticky-medium in region-us-west-2.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: enable profile objects in staging; run with internal apps (playground, internal-support) for 2 weeks. Collect telemetry and tune budgets.
2) Beta SDK release (mobile + node): expose session.create(profile) opt-in. Onboard 5 pilot customers (selected via account manager). Monitor metrics for 4 weeks.
3) Gradual ramp: expand beta to 20% of new sessions for participating accounts. Add dashboards and SLO alerts.
4) GA: enable self-serve profile creation in Console and public SDK defaults; publish pricing guidance for opt-in sessions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: cost surprise for customers who accidentally enable heavy profiles. Mitigation: SDK UI toggles default to off; server returns cost-estimate header on session.create and Console flags sessions with projected cost.
- Risk: sticky sessions create hotspots in serving pool. Mitigation: limit per-profile global budget, LRU eviction, and allow_burst gating by region.
- Risk: complex semantics leak to customers (why did my session move). Mitigation: clear evict reasons surfaced in SDK and Console and guidance doc in Console.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Persisted vs ephemeral sessions: should sessions optionally persist metadata across evictions (to auto-rehydrate)? (Action: engineering to propose storage cost delta)
- Pricing model: per-session surcharge vs included in token pricing. (Action: finance to model scenarios)
- Profile authoring: who can create custom profiles in Console? Role-based access or limit to Redwood admins initially?

Action items (next 4 weeks):
- Engineering: prototype profile objects and minimal prefetch pipeline (HOSTED-3421) by 2025-02-14 (Markus, Ravi).
- SDK: add session.create(profile) hook in JS/Swift SDKs and expose telemetry events (Priya) by 2025-02-21.
- Product: finalize initial profile defaults and pricing guidance (Lena) by 2025-02-18.
- Observability: add session-level telemetry fields and a per-profile dashboard template (Fiona) by 2025-02-28.

Appendix: short example trace (conceptual)
- t=0: client POST /sessions profile=sticky-medium -> response (session_id, sticky_cookie)
- t=20ms: server queues prefetch task; emits session.warm_start
- t=150ms: tool container warmed, session.prefetch_tokens=48, server sets session.hot_routed=true
- t=400ms: client calls tool-search via streaming; p50 latency observed 120ms vs baseline cold 320ms

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on server commitments; initial budgets should be low to avoid fleet pressure.
- Feedback requested on profile parameter names (prefetch_depth vs prefetch_tokens) and whether to expose per-tool warm targets as strings or enums.

References / links embedded: HOSTED-3421 (engineering spike), internal-playground link: https://playground.redwood.ai/session-profiles (internal), pricing-rundown draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/pricing/sticky-sessions (internal).
